references.text: Describes the same theme of fear and anxiety that fills the heart because of what the eyes see, a parallel to the madness caused by the sight of suffering.
Curses that include diseases and plagues affecting sight and mind, similar themes concerning God's judgment.
The Lord strikes the enemy's horses with confusion and madness; the same Hebrew root for madness (משגע) is used.
David pretended to be mad (משתגע), using the same word stem that describes madness in Deuteronomy 28:34.
The prophet is called mad (משגע); the same word is used to describe mental disturbance.
Elisha's servant sees the Syrian army and becomes afraid, but then sees God's army—the contrast between what the eyes see and the reaction.
